advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runner test that with `model_override` set AND `req.web=True`, the Agent kwargs OMIT `capabilities` and provenance records `web_access == "off"`.
evidence: runner.py:412 `web_requested = bool(req.web) and not self._model_override`
runner.py:409-411 comment: "The ONLY thing that can withdraw it is the injected-test-model path (`model_override`) ... every model_override test pins the byte-identical wire shape"
tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py `_agent_kwargs` constructs `PydanticAIRunner(cfg)` with NO `model_override`, so the withdrawal branch is never exercised
ABSENCE: grep of `web=True` across tests/unit hits only `web_search_capabilities(...)` helper calls and real-provider runner calls; no test combines `web=True` with a `model_override`
Existing model_override tests (test_pydantic_ai_runner.py, test_llm_failure_matrix.py, etc.) all use `web` defaulted False
advisory.finding: The new runner branch `web_requested = bool(req.web) and not self._model_override` (the injected-test-model withdrawal of web access) is untested: no test drives `req.web=True` through a runner constructed with a `model_override`. A regression dropping `and not self._model_override` would attach real WebSearch capabilities and a `native`/`local` provenance route to an injected test-model run — the exact behavior the change guarantees against — and no test would go RED.
scenarios: A future edit removes `and not self._model_override`, so an injected FunctionModel run with web=True attaches DuckDuckGo/WebSearch capabilities and records web_access as native/local instead of off — undetected by the suite.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized case to `_agent_kwargs`/the runner tests that passes `model_override=FunctionModel(...)` with `web=True` and asserts `"capabilities" not in kwargs` plus the verdict provenance `web_access == "off"`.

evidence: runner.py:645-648 comment: "the record may only claim the provider-side route when EVERY candidate can serve it — otherwise the answering model decides the route and provenance would attest by luck"
ABSENCE: grep `_intersect_capabilities` in tests/unit returns no matches; grep `native_web_search` in tests hits only single-model capability/provenance assertions, never an intersected chain
test_llm_fallback_chain.py guards the analogous temperature intersection (test_a_chain_withdraws_temperature_for_the_whole_chain) but no web-search equivalent was added
advisory.finding: The new `_intersect_capabilities` field `native_web_search=all(c.native_web_search for c in per_candidate)` is untested for a fallback chain that MIXES a native-capable and a native-incapable candidate. No test asserts that such a chain records the conservative `local`/native_web_search=False route.
scenarios: A chain of [anthropic (native), bedrock (no native)] regresses to reporting native_web_search=True (e.g. using `any` or the primary only), so the signed verdict attests a provider-side route the answering model may not have taken.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_llm_fallback_chain.py, configure a chain mixing a native-web-capable and an incapable candidate and assert the intersected caps report native_web_search=False (and web_access 'local' when web=True).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Drop the private-name `hasattr` assertion (the per-provider runner attach tests and the AST call-site guard already cover the regression) or replace it with a behavioral assertion.
evidence: tests/unit/test_web_tool_gating.py:116-118 `assert not hasattr(anthropic_mod, "_anthropic_web_search_capabilities")`
Rule-4 litmus: the assertion targets a private module attribute name, not observable behavior — a rename of any reintroduced gate helper defeats it while a same-name no-op benign symbol trips it
advisory.finding: In test_the_prefix_gated_helper_is_gone_and_the_call_site_passes_no_model, the `assert not hasattr(anthropic_mod, "_anthropic_web_search_capabilities")` clause is a change-detector on an internal private name: it breaks on a behavior-preserving reintroduction of a same-named unused symbol and cannot catch a real prefix-gate regression written under a different name. (The AST call-site half of the same test is a valid structural wiring guard.)
scenarios: A future refactor reintroduces a helper named `_anthropic_web_search_capabilities` that is unused/harmless — the test fails despite no behavior change; conversely a prefix gate reintroduced under a new name passes this clause.
